text: IL-15 is another myokine that has received considerable interest as having a potential role in skeletal muscle growth. Muscle is the primary source of IL-15 expression, and exercise regulates its production. Resistance training, in particular, has been shown to acutely elevate IL-15 protein levels, apparently through its release via microtears in muscle fibers as a result of inflammation, oxidative stress, or both (177, 186). Type II fibers show a greater increase in IL-15 mRNA levels than Type I fibers (152).
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
chapter: Chapter 1: Hypertrophy-Related Responses and Adaptations to Exercise Stress
